items.note: Phase-specific multi-agent LLM system deployed in two innovation hackathons (pilot plus follow-up); reports that phase-aligned assistance preserves idea diversity, but the comparison condition and N are not stated in the abstract (CHI extended abstract).

Rapid ideation workshop with 21 participants who brainstormed alone and with an LLM; compares variety and quality of LLM-assisted versus human ideas, within-person with no stated randomization and below 50 participants.

Two sequential behavioral experiments on generative-AI support for advertising agents, scoring fluency, flexibility, and originality, moderated by implicit theory; a further study measures viewers' attitudes to AI-assisted work; N not stated.

Within-subject comparison of breadth-first versus depth-first LLM agent designs (CoQuest) with 20 HCI researchers generating research questions; creativity is participant-perceived and quantity of questions is counted, so a rater-scored outcome is uncertain; same study as arXiv 2310.06155.

Mixed-methods study with 54 researchers using an agentic ideation system at three control levels (an AI-configuration comparison); abstract reports perceived creativity support, effort, and ownership, so outcomes may be self-report only.

Exploratory study of a children's tabletop storytelling system comparing AI-generated story-situated writing instructions with fixed prompts on writing complexity, richness, and quality; N and assignment not stated.

User studies of PersonaFlow (LLM-simulated expert personas for research ideation) report perceived relevance and creativity, critical-thinking activity, and cognitive load; no rater-scored creativity outcome in the abstract; same work as arXiv 2409.12538.

73 children aged 4 to 8 co-created oral stories with either an AI agent or a human partner; outcomes are response styles and narrative features of children's contributions, not clearly a creativity score; abstract from Semantic Scholar.

Comparative experiments on AI idea funnelling (ChatGPT, Gemini) and hybrid AI-human teams for inventive engineering design, judged on feasibility, relevance, and innovation quality; whether human participants are compared across conditions is unclear and may be model-only.

Studies of repeated human-GenAI co-creation showing joint creativity does not improve by default and that brief explanations of Idea Co-Development raise joint creativity; the retrieved abstract is a practitioner summary without design or N; AOM proceedings versions exist (10.5465/amproc.2025.227bp).
